## BOOK 1 of 3: THE O'RUDDY: A Romance
Authors: Stephen Crane and Robert Barr (1903, Frederick A. Stokes). Gutenberg #29573. Frontispiece by C. D. Williams. Narrator: Tom (The O'Ruddy), first-person.

**Ch I**
- Narrator's ancestors lived at Glandore (Co. Cork, near Old Head of Kinsale). Father dies, ~age 18 narrator. Father's dying words: "Tom... never be civil to a king's officer... red coat, rogue." Two swords: grand one from King Louis, plain one. Cask of brandy. Ship "Martha Bixby". Papers belonging to young Lord Strepp (now Earl of Westport, London); lent breeches in France campaign ("he would have gone bare"). Estate left to old Mickey Clancy; priest Father Donovan (also "Father O'Donovan").
- Bristol inn: fat landlord in white apron. Supper: garrulous man in plum-colour; Lord Strepp (~20, fair unpowdered hair), Colonel Royale (~40, clear-eyed soldierly), Forister (dark-skinned, proud). Colonel tells breeches story; narrator shouts "That, sir, is a lie," gives lie twice ("We are never obliged to give it twice in my country").
- Strepp visits: duel arranged at daybreak. Narrator says friend will attend (a lie). Colonel's apology.
- Forister brags about Irish with clubs; narrator boxes his ear, kicks him out the front door into the yard. Earl of Westport (tall, "old eagle") and two ladies (one with bright liquid eyes) present; Earl says "Come to my chamber in the morning, O'Ruddy." Colonel and Strepp seen laughing over railing.

**Ch II**
- Narrator finds red-headed Irish vagabond Paddy (keening, from Ireland); dresses him in narrator's blue velvet, flowered waistcoat, pink stockings, cocked hat, sword of King Louis on string around neck. Paddy's "lashings" proposal confuses Strepp. Duel on green turf: narrator laughs in Colonel's face; wounds Colonel in sword arm; Strepp stops it ("Back, Colonel!"). Narrator refuses to kill him ("Damme if I will!"). Crowd of boys; Paddy's hair.

**Ch III**
- Papers stolen by Paddy (he took them; "one badly worn at the heel"). Narrator suspects Forister. Landlord says Forister went to Bath. Narrator rides; highwayman Jem Bottles (ballads in Bristol and Bath; mother, Dame Bottles; seven ballads Bristol, three Bath; "snuff-boxes"; "Little Susan" and eggs). Jem's horses at mother's cottage; narrator borrows five? guineas; Jem gets 14 guineas, narrator 1 (from Bottles' store, total 15).

**Ch IV**
- Narrator dreams of Lady Mary (Earl's daughter), realizes love. Bath: Forister gone back to Bristol. Wayside inn: Paddy had barricaded Forister in a room ("Red Giant" / "little black man"); narrator enters; Forister's threats.

**Ch V**
- Forister denies stealing papers; laughs. Nell (Bristol girl) mentioned. Jem's "muzzle-faced" insult. Paddy's hair insulted. Back in Bristol: Earl sends for narrator; Earl (bed, rasping voice) says papers "worthless... straw". Lady Mary, daughter. Narrator's sword scabbard tinkles. Earl calls narrator "rogue". 

**Ch VI**
- Papers fall from Earl's pillows; narrator takes them, flings sword at Strepp's feet, gives papers to Lady Mary with bow. Strepp & Colonel; Colonel vows backing. Forister's "God spare you" motif appears later. Narrator learns Forister is father's partner in shipping, Lord Strepp's family fond of him; Forister is "one of the finest swordsmen in England." Colonel Clarence Royale (name revealed). Narrator's Countess (mother) later.

**Ch VII**
- Narrator thinks about Glandore, Mickey Clancy, estate. Forister visits: "I have decided to kill you." Forister's "Nell" and "the child" (Bristol girl); narrator bluffs.

**Ch VIII**
- Colonel beats hand on wall; narrator talks of Ponsonby & Stewart duel. Strepp and Colonel comically bow. Countess and Lady Mary in garden; parrot shouts "Pretty lady!" Countess has parrot removed; "I cannot endure parrots." Lady Mary approaches narrator: "don't fight with Forister in the morning. 'Tis certain death."; narrator proud; she: "I did not wish you to suppose that I ever failed to pay a debt."

**Ch IX**
- Father's story (Mickey, lancer, "The lance of the lancer"). Colonel's note from Lady Mary: "God spare you!" Colonel was cornet in Earl's regiment; saw Mary as a baby in bath. Duel at dawn with Forister (Lord Strepp second). Narrator wounds Forister in left shoulder; Forister tries to throw sword.

**Ch X**
- Narrator famous; Countess of Westport chases him around table and chairs in coffee-room; "misapprehension"; ivory fan hits bystander.

**Ch XI**
- Narrator sees Forister carried on pallet. Westport party leaves Bristol. Narrator goes to Bath; horse lamed in puddle. Finds Paddy and Jem in haycock stealing Earl's carriage (papers and guineas; Paddy's "Dear Sister Mary" letter). Jem and Paddy robbed Earl's carriage; narrator takes papers and "philanthropist" share of gold.

**Ch XII**
- Narrator back in Bath; Earl's chamber; "The papers are in the breast of my coat." Earl's offers; "Lady Mary Strepp" as true owner.

**Ch XIII**
- Earl: "Why didn't you read the papers?" Narrator: would hire tutor in London. Earl knows of narrator's love. Countess storms room; Paddy in fight with Countess (chair against wall); narrator flees.

**Ch XIV**
- Paddy pins Countess with chair; narrator escapes under bed; leave to London.

**Ch XV**
- Ride to London with Paddy; Paddy's ideas of English gentlemen; Father Corrigan.

**Ch XVI**
- Narrator plays "sticadoro proderodo sliceriscum" test on Jem; training servants to stand with bottles; gentlemanly drill.

**Ch XVII**
- London entry; "Pig and Turnip" inn in Bishopsgate Street; mug-house; Fullbil (old literary master), Bobbs (dramatist), Fancher (critic), Doctor Chord (little scientist, pleasant). Chord shows Lady Mary; "Red Slipper" mug-house.

**Ch XVIII–XIX**
- Fullbil's club: "Ireland is not in Italy"; mocks Irish; narrator's story of Galway. Paddy and Jem at "Red Slipper" singing ballad; Paddy's "loriot" bird talk with valet.

**Ch XX–XXII**
- Sunday in Kensington Gardens; Doctor Chord gossips; sees Lady Mary; Chord reports Earl's illness; narrator plans climbing wall at Earl's house.

**Ch XXIII–XXVI**
- Climbing tree; gardener "Strammers" with blunderbuss; Lady Mary says "I'm afraid it's l-l-loaded"; narrator proposes love. Strammers befriended by Paddy & Jem. Chord warns about papers; theft plot.

**Ch XXVII–XXIX**
- Sunday raid on Earl's garden; Paddy and Jem beaten by footmen; narrator meets Lady Mary in locked boudoir; she gives advice; kiss; Lady Mary says papers represent law. Father Donovan in London (St. Patrick chapel). Temple lawyer Josiah Brooks; 500 guineas advanced; Brede estate (Sussex, near Rye).

**Ch XXX–XXXI**
- Brooks, Temple, guineas. Night attack by 9 ruffians with swords (narrator disarms them with knife tricks; "Mr. O'Ruddy, these swords are yours"). Journey to Rye with Father Donovan; Jem robs Earl's men on road (Dr. Chord among them); highwaymen "Stand and deliver."

**Ch XXXII–XXXIII**
- Rye, Tom Peel and nine men; Brede House seized; caretaker; Sir Goddard Oxenbridge ghost lore; tunnel; Lord Strepp attacks, captured in tunnel, parley; Earl and Countess at Manor House; Countess slaps narrator. Lady Mary consents. Marriage by Father Donovan; children Patrick, Mary, Terence, Kathleen, Michael, Bridget, Donovan.

## BOOK 2 of 3: THE BOY TRADERS; OR, THE SPORTSMAN'S CLUB AMONG THE BOERS
Author: Harry Castlemon (Frank Nelson Series). Gutenberg #56868. Publisher Henry T. Coates & Co., Philadelphia.

**Characters:** Captain "Uncle Dick" (sailor, Stranger schooner); Frank Nelson (nephew, sailing-master); Walter Gaylord (paymaster; brother Eugene); Archie Winters (cousin of Frank, bold, witty); Fred Craven; George Le Dell; Perk (Phil Perkins); Featherweight; Jasper Babcock; Dick Lewis (trapper, backwoods, fast, Indian-yell; "Human natur'!"); Bob Kelly (old trapper); Mr. Baldwin (first mate); Mr. Parker (second mate); Lucas and Barton (boatswain's mates); Freas; Rodgers; the Doctor (negro cook); Brown (repentant sailor); Tom Peel (giant captain); Mr. Wilbur (sheep-herder, friend); Waters (escaped convict giant, "Stand by me, mates"); Fowler (consul's clerk, scheming, gold eyeglass); Bob (ticket-of-leave man); Mack (McGregor, Scotch transport-rider/driver, runs away); Mynheer Schrader (surly Boer field cornet); Kaffirs; Zulus; Griquas; the English colonel (outfit seller); Chase & Wilson (absent friends); Kendall (midshipman); Lieutenant (gray-headed, English war steamer).

**Plot events in order:**
- Ch I: Sandwich Islands; Honolulu; Frank's sailing lessons; surf-board swimming at Hilo; Kilauea volcano; trappers fear.
- Ch II: Gale; Stranger shells natives on Mangrove Islands (Long Tom 30-pounder); cyclone; schooner dismantled.
- Ch III: Long Tom thrown overboard; ship lost on reef; survivors rescued (eleven saved); convicts among them (Waters, three others).
- Ch IV: Plan to Hobart Town; convicts suspected; Archie and Frank talk.
- Ch V: Waters attacks Lucas; Dick Lewis subdues him; Waters in irons.
- Ch VI: Arrive Hobart Town (Tasmania); Fowler (consul's clerk) demands the men; police take convicts.
- Ch VII: Australia trip; horse-race Dick vs Eugene's horse (Dick wins); Fowler's visit; Frank locked in cabin; schooner seized by convicts (Waters, Bob, Fowler).
- Ch VIII: Frank learns Fowler & Bob plan; Waters explains; Archie captured by mistake (Bob grabs Archie, not Walter).
- Ch IX: Archie tells Frank; Frank runs schooner past steamer (Yankee trick); "I wasn't born."
- Ch X: Archie handcuffs Waters while asleep; Frank recaptures schooner; Fowler ironed; Doctor guards; Brown & crew repentant. British lieutenant and midshipman Kendall; Frank refuses to haul colours; American flag.
- Ch XI: Frank obstinate; Club rejoins on tug; three foremast hands discharged; Stranger sails to Natal.
- Ch XII: Natal; Scotch driver Mack; English colonel's outfit (oxen, wagon, salted horses, double-barrels); lots drawn: Frank gets #3 (ugly horse, heavy rifle); Archie gets silver-mounted rifle and thoroughbred. Kaffir cook.
- Ch XIII: Boer Mynheer Schrader refuses trade; Frank repairs Griqua gun; "Mr. Jones"; Eugene's dare; lion veldt.
- Ch XIV: Night in shooting-pit by fountain: Archie, Fred, Eugene shoot at what they think are lions; actually wild dogs.
- Ch XV: Archie's horse stuck in thorn wood; Mack's suspicious behaviour; Kaffirs desert.
- Ch XVI: Mack steals Walter's horse and gun, flees; Kaffirs desert; Griquas; Zulu delegation demands; Dick's "medicine-man" Indian yells scare Zulus off.
- Ch XVII: Zulu ambush in dry stream; Archie's horse killed; Frank saves Archie (spear through haversack); return journey; ivory; Christmas return to Bellville; family reunion; epilogue (Frank lawyer, Archie civil engineer, Fred revenue lieutenant, etc.).

## BOOK 3 of 3: A LITTLE IRISH GIRL
Author: J. M. Callwell (Blackie & Son, London/Glasgow). Gutenberg #75934. Frontispiece "There's thim that'll not forgit it." Narrator: third person, focus on Norah O'Brien.

**Characters:** Norah O'Brien (~11, short, dark hair, Irish blue eyes, shabby black mourning dress, mischievous); Anstace O'Brien (eldest sister, governess to Dr. Trafford family); Roderick O'Brien (brother, ~21, lawyer's clerk, cough; "tall, dark-haired"); Manus O'Brien (~12, brother at school, Dr. Ford's, Kent; diphtheria sent home); Piers O'Brien (father, writer, died autumn/six months before); Marion Belthorpe (mother, deceased; eloped with Piers); Uncle Nicholas O'Brien (of Moyross Abbey, copper mine); Harry Wyndham (grand-nephew) and Ella Wyndham (his sister); Miss Browne (governess, "Brownie"); Cousin Ansey (Anstace O'Brien, died; asylum in Dublin); Hugh Masters (lost fiancé); Lily Allardyce (school friend); Miss Clarksons (Euphemia, Susan, eldest Miss Clarkson); Fräulein Glock; Biddy (housekeeper, sister of Tom Hogan); Tom Hogan (coachman/gardener/steward); Lanty Hogan (red-headed nephew, poacher, makes potheen); Bride (Lanty's sister, maid); Connor (driver); Mr. Lynch (rector) and Mrs. Lynch; M'Bain (Scotch mine manager); Malachy Flanagan (red-bearded, orator, still-owner); Captain Charles Lester R.M.; Lady Louisa Butler (Dromore); Cartwright (butler); Dr. Hanlon; Mrs. Connor and Thady (pigs); Pat Lannigan (gamekeeper).

**Events in order:**
- Ch I: Treherne House school (Miss Clarksons); geography lesson; Norah sent to bottom; Lily's Paris trip; Norah's father Piers dead; Anstace's message of inheritance coming.
- Ch II: Cousin Ansey's legacy: Kilshane (small house, ~£100/yr, two miles from Moyross); Uncle Nicholas's feud; Anstace explains Marion's elopement and Nicholas's wrath.
- Ch III: Norah's freak: toboggan down stairs on tea-tray with Lily; Miss Clarkson kisses Norah; Norah's Irish speech.
- Ch IV: Norah's last days; journey to Ireland; arrival at Kilshane in rain; Tom and Biddy welcome.
- Ch V: Kilshane kitchen (hens, kittens, dog); Anstace cleans; Biddy's stories of Miss Ansey; Lanty brings fish.
- Ch VI: Rector Lynch; mine dispute; Manus arrives; Norah drives to Ballyfin with Connor; Ella's pony Sheila runs away; Roderick catches it at gate; Ella (Wyndham) visits Kilshane; Miss Browne appears (bonnet backwards).
- Ch VII: Miss Browne's background; Ella & Miss Browne return; Nicholas sees Marion's portrait; Ella learns Piers' portrait is Marion.
- Ch VIII: Ballintaggart Cave seal hunt; Norah eavesdrops; Lanty & Manus; Manus kills seal (rips sleeve); Norah confronts.
- Ch IX: Row home; Monk's Walk ghost (table-cloth with holes; Miss Browne scolds laundry-maid); Manus's shot at ghost (actually a table-cloth).
- Ch X: Captain Lester R.M. announced; dinner mishaps (Bride, Biddy); Lester plans raid on Drinane Head still.
- Ch XI: Norah awakens early, climbs Drinane Head alone to warn Lanty; Malachy Flanagan's still; Norah disguised with shawl.
- Ch XII: Lester & Roderick raid, fail; Malachy carries Norah home on back; Norah lies to Roderick and Anstace.
- Ch XIII: Roderick & Anstace at Dromore; Manus & Norah visit mine; Malachy harangues miners; miners march on Moyross; Norah & Manus run to warn.
- Ch XIV: Attack on Moyross; Norah in abbey window with quilt & candle as "White Nun"; crowd flees; Norah falls and is hurt; Uncle Nicholas returns; Nicholas: "Piers' child".
- Ch XV: Norah unconscious; Anstace and Roderick arrive from Dromore; Nicholas calls Anstace "Marion".
- Ch XVI: Norah recovers; Nicholas reconciles; Harry to army; Roderick to manage mine and marry Ella; Lanty made under-keeper; Norah reveals secret; Anstace & Norah move to Moyross; "Norah's idea" and triumphant close.
